IL1.1: Define a clear Lean strategic vision with precise operational objectives and communicate it at every level of the organisation.
IL1.2: Allocate a dedicated budget to support Lean improvement projects and make it a key part of the annual financial plan.
IL1.3: Take an active part in Lean initiatives, for example by sponsoring Kaizen events.
IL1.4: Communicate openly about the progress of Lean initiatives, including successes and lessons learned.
IL1.5: Take personal responsibility for the results of Lean initiatives and report on them regularly.

IL2.1: Run awareness campaigns so that Lean principles are understood and accepted across the company.
IL2.2: Encourage and develop transformational leadership through dedicated training and role models.
IL2.3: Identify and actively manage resistance to change by offering suitable training and support.
IL2.4: Build Lean principles into HR processes and evaluation criteria.
IL2.5: Recognise and reward behaviours and results that are in line with the Lean culture.

IL3.1: Adapt strategic communication to support and highlight Lean initiatives.
IL3.2: Tailor internal communication so that it is consistent with Lean principles and easy to understand.
IL3.3: Build active listening into management processes to encourage continuous improvement.
IL3.4: Communicate regularly on the progress of Lean initiatives at every level of the company.
IL3.5: Design communication training that takes the specifics of Lean into account.

IL4.1: Make sure every employee receives basic training in Lean principles.
IL4.2: Offer advanced training to develop Lean-specific skills.
IL4.3: Set up a Lean certification programme to validate the skills acquired.
IL4.4: Update Lean training content regularly so it reflects the latest best practices.
IL4.5: Assess employees' Lean skills to make sure they are able to lead improvement projects.

IL5.1: Train employees to a thorough knowledge of Lean tools so that initiatives are effective.
IL5.2: Encourage the proper use of Lean tools through workshops and experience sharing.
IL5.3: Make the necessary resources, such as relevant software and databases, easy to access.
IL5.4: Stimulate innovation in the use of Lean tools through idea-incubation programmes and internal challenges.
IL5.5: Periodically assess and update technical Lean skills to ensure operational excellence.

IL6.1: Encourage employees to take an active part in Lean initiatives and to contribute their ideas.
IL6.2: Promote shared responsibility by making teams jointly accountable for Lean results.
IL6.3: Give employees the autonomy to make decisions about process improvement.
IL6.4: Adapt training to strengthen employee engagement in Lean initiatives.
IL6.5: Recognise and reward significant contributions to the success of Lean projects.

IL7.1: Value in-depth knowledge of Lean principles as a key factor in career progression.
IL7.2: Encourage the development of Lean-specific technical skills through suitable career paths.
IL7.3: Make it easy to share Lean expertise through communities of practice and collaboration platforms.
IL7.4: Personalise training paths to meet specific Lean skill-development needs.
IL7.5: Formally recognise Lean certifications and include them in performance and promotion criteria.
